subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: The Wedge: Splitting the World
description: A quick, practical guide to The Wedge: Splitting the World.

hook.text: An axe head is a wedge. So is a knife blade, a chisel, and your front teeth.

buildup.text: A wedge converts a force applied to its blunt end into perpendicular forces that push outward on two sides.

discovery.text: Thinner wedges have greater mechanical advantage. A razor blade splits material with almost zero applied force.

twist.text: The earliest stone tools, 3.3 million years old, are crude wedges. They predate the genus Homo by 700,000 years.

climax.text: Modern hydraulic wedges split rock for mining and demolition. A small pump exerts thousands of tons of splitting force.

punchline.text: Push forward. Split sideways. The oldest tool on Earth.

quiz.question: Why do thinner wedges have greater mechanical advantage?
options: They penetrate deeper with each strike, moving more material
The shallow angle converts more forward force into outward splitting force
They weigh less, allowing faster repeated strikes
